entry.title: fastgpt-mcpCLient未认证ssrf复现
entry.content:
漏洞介绍

/api/support/mcp/client/ 下的 getTools 与 runTool 两个端点均接收请求体中的 url 并由服务器主动向其发起 MCP/SSE 连接。两接口均无任何鉴权、url 完全由请求者控制、连接结果（拒绝/超时/HTTP 状态码/响应内容类型）以错误消息形式回显 —— 构成未认证 SSRF 与内网测绘 oracle

gettools接口的作用是mcp我收+拉取工具列表

runtool接口的作用是mcp握手+调用指定工具并返回执行结果

下面主要讲的是代码审计相关的东西

代码审计

代码审计已FastGPT-4.13.0版本为例

下载链接：https://github.com/labring/FastGPT/archive/refs/tags/v4.13.0.zip

理解项目架构

FastGPT 是一个 Next.js + TypeScript + MongoDB (Mongoose) 的 monorepo 项目

发现可疑目录

projects/app/src/pages/api/support/mcp/client

审计思考 ②：support/ 目录在 FastGPT 里放的是”支撑功能”（用户、团队、外链、文件等），这里的 mcp/client 从命名看是”FastGPT 作为 MCP 客户端去连接别人的 MCP 服务器” —— 与 core/app/mcpTools（把别人注册的 MCP 工具跑起来）职责相近但路径完全不同。每个文件一个端点，先看 getTools.ts。

看到gettools.ts的代码内容

看看这个代码大概的意思

NextAPI(handler)

NextAPI 是错误处理包装器，是否附带鉴权要去 middleware/entry.ts 确认

body = { url, headerSecret }

url 是请求体里的普通字段 —— 类型标注 string 只是编译期约束，运行时传什么就是什么

const { url } = req.body

用户输入原样解构，无 Zod/无白名单/无内网地址校验

new MCPClient({ url, ... })

用户可控的 url 即将交给服务器去连接 —— SSRF 的经典形态

headerSecret → headers

headerSecret 经过 getSecretValue 处理后，会作为 HTTP 请求头发送给目标 url

getTools() 结果直接返回

连接结果（成功/失败细节）回显给请求者 ，所以这里会返回错误的代码后续可以用来区分正确与错误的消息

到这里已经具备 SSRF 的全部要素：用户可控目标 + 服务器主动发起连接 + 结果回显。缺的只是一个确认：这个端点到底有没有鉴权？没有 req 传给任何 auth* 函数，但没有显式拒绝也可能是全局中间件拦的 —— 必须排掉这个可能。

鉴权检查

FastGPT 的 API 包装器在 projects/app/src/service/middleware/entry.ts：

FastGPT 的 API 包装器在 projects/app/src/service/middleware/entry.ts：

beforeCallback 是每个请求进来前依次执行的函数数组 —— FastGPT 所有需要登录的端点，都是把 authCert（Cookie/API Key 校验）这类函数放进各自文件的 beforeCallback 或在 handler 里显式调用。对比一个正常需要鉴权的端点（如 core/chat/getHistories.ts 内部）：

而 getTools.ts 的 handler 全文（第二步）没有出现任何 auth 字样，beforeCallback 又是空数组。两条路都排除后可以下结论：

鉴权结论：/api/support/mcp/client/getTools 无任何身份验证 —— 未登录、无 Cookie、无 API Key 均可直接调用。

顺手确认 runTool.ts与全局是否有其他拦截（Nginx 层的 WAF 因部署而异，代码层无拦截）。

读 runTool.ts

现在回到projects/app/src/pages/api/support/mcp/client

与 getTools 完全同构：无鉴权 + url 直通。差异是交互更深一层 —— toolName 与 params 会作为 MCP 协议的 tools/call 参数发到目标服务器，执行结果原样返回给请求者

两个端点、同一根因（无鉴权 + URL 直通）

审计总结

根据上面两个接口没有任何鉴权以及用户可以自由控制请求路径还有服务端会返回请求结果的表现来看，两个接口存在ssrf漏洞

攻击者构造如下请求包就可以探测内网

请求包（getTools）

响应（服务器真实访问了内网沙箱并读取响应头）：

请求包（runTools）

响应（与 getTools 完全一致的回显 oracle）：

runTool 相对 getTools 的增量：toolName 与 params 完全可控 —— 当 url 指向内网真实 MCP 服务时可发起协议级工具调用；指向攻击者服务器时可在 body 中携带任意 arguments（同系列目标已用 webhook.site 实证：两接口均产生 GET+POST 成对回连，UA=node，来源 IP 为目标服务器本身）。

判定逻辑：可达目标返回”内容类型/证书校验”错误、关闭端口返回”ECONNREFUSED + IP:端口”，两类响应可区分且均由服务器侧产生 → 两接口 SSRF 均成立

实战案例

实际测试下来发现

用 mcp/client getTools 对目标内网地址段做系统化探测，每种网络状态都有可区分的回显：

探测地址回显状态判定
http://127.0.0.1:3000connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3000闭合（精确回显 IP:端口）
http://127.0.0.1:3001/3002/27017/6379/80/443/47654全部 ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:<端口>逐端口闭合确认
http://172.18.0.1:3000Invalid content type开放（HTTP 服务，非 MCP）
http://172.18.0.1:3000/definitely-not-exist-xyzNon-200 status code (404)开放且服务指纹可读（404 应答）
http://172.18.0.1:3001connect ECONNREFUSED 172.18.0.1:3001同主机闭合端口
http://172.18.0.1:27017connect ECONNREFUSED 172.18.0.1:27017同主机闭合端口
http://172.17.0.1:80/3000/3001/3005/3306无回显（超时）被过滤（与闭合状态明确区分）
http://10.0.0.1:80无回显（超时）被过滤/不可达
http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/无回显（超时）云元数据被防火墙过滤

结论：三种网络状态（开放/闭合/被过滤）通过不同回显完全可区分，且在同一内网主机（172.18.0.1）上实现了逐端口判别 —— 该 SSRF 是一个完整的内网端口扫描与服务指纹识别 oracle，实测即发现了内网开放服务 172.18.0.1:3000

entry.title: FastGPT MCP Client Unauthenticated SSRF Reproduction
entry.content:
Vulnerability Introduction

The getTools and runTool endpoints under /api/support/mcp/client/ both accept a url from the request body and have the server proactively initiate an MCP/SSE connection to it. Both endpoints have no authentication whatsoever, the url is fully controlled by the requester, and the connection result (refused / timeout / HTTP status code / response content type) is echoed back in the form of error messages — constituting an unauthenticated SSRF and intranet mapping oracle.

The getTools endpoint performs the MCP handshake + pulls the tool list.

The runTool endpoint performs the MCP handshake + invokes the specified tool and returns the execution result.

What follows mainly covers the code-audit side of things.

Code Audit

The code audit uses FastGPT 4.13.0 as an example.

Download link: https://github.com/labring/FastGPT/archive/refs/tags/v4.13.0.zip

Understanding the Project Architecture

FastGPT is a Next.js + TypeScript + MongoDB (Mongoose) monorepo project.

Discovering a Suspicious Directory

projects/app/src/pages/api/support/mcp/client

Audit thought ②: The support/ directory in FastGPT holds “supporting features” (users, teams, external links, files, etc.). Judging by its name, the mcp/client here means “FastGPT acting as an MCP client connecting to someone else’s MCP server” — similar in responsibility to core/app/mcpTools (which runs the MCP tools registered by others) but on a completely different path. One endpoint per file, so let’s look at getTools.ts first.

Looking at the code content of getTools.ts:

Let’s walk through what this code roughly means.

NextAPI(handler)

NextAPI is an error-handling wrapper; whether it attaches authentication must be confirmed in middleware/entry.ts.

body = { url, headerSecret }

url is just an ordinary field in the request body — the string type annotation is only a compile-time constraint; at runtime whatever you pass is what it gets.

const { url } = req.body

User input is destructured as-is — no Zod, no allowlist, no intranet-address validation.

new MCPClient({ url, ... })

The user-controlled url is about to be handed to the server to connect to — the classic shape of an SSRF.

headerSecret → headers

After being processed by getSecretValue, headerSecret is sent as HTTP request headers to the target url.

The result of getTools() is returned directly

The connection result (success/failure details) is echoed back to the requester, so the error messages returned here can later be used to distinguish correct from incorrect responses.

At this point every ingredient of SSRF is present: user-controlled target + server-initiated connection + result echo. All that’s missing is one confirmation: does this endpoint actually have authentication? No req is passed to any auth* function, but the absence of an explicit rejection could also mean a global middleware is intercepting — that possibility must be ruled out.

Authentication Check

FastGPT’s API wrapper lives in projects/app/src/service/middleware/entry.ts:

FastGPT’s API wrapper lives in projects/app/src/service/middleware/entry.ts:

beforeCallback is an array of functions executed in sequence before every request comes in — all FastGPT endpoints that require login put functions like authCert (Cookie/API Key validation) into their own file’s beforeCallback or call them explicitly inside the handler. For comparison, a normal endpoint that does require authentication (e.g., inside core/chat/getHistories.ts):

Meanwhile, the full text of the getTools.ts handler (step two) contains no auth wording at all, and beforeCallback is an empty array. With both paths ruled out, we can conclude:

Authentication conclusion: /api/support/mcp/client/getTools has no authentication whatsoever — it can be called directly with no login, no Cookie, and no API Key.

While we’re at it, confirm runTool.ts and whether anything else intercepts globally (an Nginx-layer WAF varies by deployment; there is no interception at the code layer).

Reading runTool.ts

Now back to projects/app/src/pages/api/support/mcp/client

Completely isomorphic to getTools: no authentication + the url passed straight through. The difference is that the interaction goes one level deeper — toolName and params are sent to the target server as the arguments of the MCP protocol’s tools/call, and the execution result is returned as-is to the requester.

Two endpoints, one root cause (no authentication + URL pass-through)

Audit Summary

Given that the two endpoints above have no authentication whatsoever, the user can freely control the request path, and the server returns the request result, both endpoints have an SSRF vulnerability.

An attacker can probe the intranet by crafting the following request packets:

Request packet (getTools)

Response (the server actually visited the intranet sandbox and read its response headers):

Request packet (runTool)

Response (an echo oracle identical to getTools):

runTool’s increment over getTools: toolName and params are fully controllable — when url points to a real intranet MCP service, protocol-level tool calls can be initiated; when it points to an attacker-controlled server, arbitrary arguments can be carried in the body (verified empirically against targets of the same series via webhook.site: both endpoints produced paired GET+POST callbacks, UA=node, with the source IP being the target server itself).

Determination logic: reachable targets return “content type/certificate validation” errors, closed ports return “ECONNREFUSED + IP:port”; the two response classes are distinguishable and both are produced server-side → the SSRF holds on both endpoints.

Real-World Case

What actual testing revealed:

Using mcp/client getTools to systematically probe the target’s intranet address range, every network state yields a distinguishable echo:

Probe addressEchoStatus determination
http://127.0.0.1:3000connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3000Closed (precise IP:port echo)
http://127.0.0.1:3001/3002/27017/6379/80/443/47654All ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:<port>Port-by-port closed confirmation
http://172.18.0.1:3000Invalid content typeOpen (HTTP service, not MCP)
http://172.18.0.1:3000/definitely-not-exist-xyzNon-200 status code (404)Open with readable service fingerprint (404)
http://172.18.0.1:3001connect ECONNREFUSED 172.18.0.1:3001Closed port on the same host
http://172.18.0.1:27017connect ECONNREFUSED 172.18.0.1:27017Closed port on the same host
http://172.17.0.1:80/3000/3001/3005/3306No echo (timeout)Filtered (clearly distinct from closed)
http://10.0.0.1:80No echo (timeout)Filtered / unreachable
http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/No echo (timeout)Cloud metadata blocked by firewall

Conclusion: the three network states (open/closed/filtered) are fully distinguishable through different echoes, and port-by-port discrimination was achieved against the same intranet host (172.18.0.1) — this SSRF is a complete intranet port-scanning and service-fingerprinting oracle; in actual testing it immediately revealed the open intranet service 172.18.0.1:3000.

entry.title: CVE-2026-79483-EN
entry.content:
CVE-2026-79483: FastGPT NoSQL Injection — Unauthenticated Access to Chat History Titles of All Users Across the Platform

Vulnerability Overview

Here is a brief introduction to the vulnerability

The affected product is https://github.com/labring/FastGPT, which has 29.5K stars as of now. The affected version range is >= 4.10.0 and <= 4.14.0. The POST /api/core/chat/getHistories endpoint contains a NoSQL injection vulnerability. An unauthenticated attacker can inject NoSQL operators ($ne, $regex, $gt, etc.) via a crafted JSON payload to bypass the outLink permission check, thereby gaining unauthorized access to the chat history titles of all users across the entire platform

To be honest, this was not originally found through white-box code auditing. At the very beginning, it was actually discovered through black-box vulnerability hunting, and the code audit only started after I noticed the target was running FastGPT

The following content mainly covers discovering the vulnerability through code auditing, comparing old and new versions, and real-world cases

Code Audit

The code audit uses FastGPT version 4.13.0 as an example

Download link: https://github.com/labring/FastGPT/archive/refs/tags/v4.13.0.zip

Understanding the Project Architecture

FastGPT is a Next.js + TypeScript + MongoDB (Mongoose) monorepo project

When auditing a MongoDB application, the core question we need to focus on is:

Is user input directly concatenated into a MongoDB query object without filtering out operator keys starting with $?

This is the most common security vulnerability pattern in MongoDB + Node.js applications

First, let’s understand the architecture of this project

Audit Tip ①: In a Next.js project, every file under the pages/api/ directory is an API endpoint. The file path is the route path. This is your audit entry checklist

In a Mongoose application, the data flow is typically:

Audit goal: verify at every layer whether user input is properly validated and sanitized before it flows into database queries.

Locating the API Entry Point

As mentioned before, the point to audit is getHistories.ts, located at FastGPT-4.13.0/projects/app/src/pages/api/core/chat/getHistories.ts

This file is an API interface in the backend processing logic

So we start looking at the code in getHistories.ts

In the code before const { offset, pageSize } = parsePaginationRequest(req);, several rules are defined: URL parameter rules, request body rules, response data rules, handler rules, and data extraction rules. The line const { offset, pageSize } = parsePaginationRequest(req); just parses the two parameters offset and pageSize, nothing worth dwelling on

Next we arrive at a key piece of code

Specifically looking at

If shareId and outLinkUid exist, the authOutLink function is executed and returns uid, and then the value of outLinkUid in the match object is replaced with the uid just obtained

Having audited up to here, some problems become quite obvious

Problem 1: req.body is destructured directly with no Zod/schema validation, so the user can pass arbitrary JSON types (objects, arrays, etc.)

Problem 2: shareId is written directly into the match object. If shareId is {"$ne": ""}, MongoDB will interpret it as an operator

Problem 3: outLinkUid: uid — uid comes from authOutLink(), so we need to trace whether the uid returned by this function is safe

So we start auditing the authOutLink function

Tracing the Authentication Chain: authOutLink

authOutLink is called to validate shareId and outLinkUid. Open FastGPT-4.13.0/projects/app/src/service/support/permission/auth/outLink.ts:

For this code, what we specifically need to look at is obviously the part where the authOutLink function is defined

This code fragment

defines that the incoming shareId, outLinkUid have the data type ShareChatAuthProps, and the return type is a Promise

Then we go straight to the handling logic for the existence of outLinkUid

const result = await authOutLinkValid({ shareId }); — this line clearly shows that shareId is passed to the authOutLinkValid function for processing, and after processing we get the result variable

Moving on

The authOutLinkInit function is called with outLinkUid (the outLink credential provided by the user) and hookUrl (the validation API address), and uid (the real user ID) is extracted from the returned result

So for this piece of code, are there two validations — one is authOutLinkValid and the other is authOutLinkInit? Their validations are closely intertwined: authOutLinkValid takes shareId and outputs result, while authOutLinkInit takes outLinkUid and values related to result and outputs the final uid we need

Having audited up to here, several more problems were found

Problem 1: The emptiness check on outLinkUid, if (!outLinkUid) — if the input is an object, the truthy check can be bypassed

Problem 2: We need to specifically audit the handling logic of authOutLinkValid and authOutLinkInit next

Tracing the Authentication Chain: authOutLinkValid

Location of the function

packages/service/support/permission/publish/authLink.ts

The specific code is as follows

This code is very straightforward: in const outLinkConfig = await MongoOutLink.findOne({ shareId }).lean<OutLinkSchema<T>>();, the precondition that shareId must not be empty can certainly be satisfied, and after that findOne is executed to query the database. The critical point is that there is no restriction on shareId, which allows an attacker to directly construct MongoDB operators

Finally, it returns an object containing two things:

  1. appId: the application ID extracted from outLinkConfig (a string)
  2. outLinkConfig: the complete share link configuration object (containing all fields)

Tracing the Authentication Chain: authOutLinkInit

Location of the function

projects/app/src/service/support/permission/auth/outLink.ts

In the community edition, return Promise.resolve({ uid: data.outLinkUid }) directly puts data.outLinkUid as-is into the uid field and returns it — no type validation, no length check, no character filtering whatsoever. Since outLinkUid is directly controlled by the user, this results in NoSQL injection

Finally, back to gethistories.ts

Building the match object

match = {shareId: {"$ne":""},outLinkUid: {"$ne":""},updateTime: { $gte: ... }}

Finally the query is executed based on match

And it returns the chat data of all users across the entire platform

Audit Summary

Step 1: The attacker sends a malicious request

text

Step 2: getHistories.ts destructures the parameters

text

Step 3: authOutLink → authOutLinkValid({ shareId })

text

Step 4: authOutLink → authOutLinkInit({ outLinkUid })

text

Step 5: getHistories.ts builds the match object

text

Step 6: MongoDB executes the query

text

Real-World Example

Since the developers did not add authCert, the endpoint is directly exposed, so it can be exploited right away

entry.title: CVE-2026-79483
entry.content:
CVE-2026-79483: FastGPT NoSQL 注入 — 未授权访问全平台用户聊天历史标题

漏洞介绍

漏洞的简单介绍如下

存在漏洞的产品https://github.com/labring/FastGPT截止目前有29.5K星标，受影响的版本范围`>= 4.10.0且<= 4.14.0，POST /api/core/chat/getHistories 端点存在 **NoSQL 注入**漏洞。**未认证**攻击者可以通过构造恶意 JSON 载荷注入 NoSQL 操作符（$ne、$regex、$gt` 等）来绕过 outLink 权限校验，从而未授权访问全平台所有用户的聊天记录标题

其实这个最开始并不是进行白盒审计出来的，一开始实际上是进行黑盒漏洞挖掘挖出来的，发现使用的是fastgpt之后才开始的代码审计

下面的内容就主要开始代码审计发现漏洞，新旧版本对比，真实案例

代码审计

代码审计已FastGPT-4.13.0版本为例

下载链接：https://github.com/labring/FastGPT/archive/refs/tags/v4.13.0.zip

理解项目架构

FastGPT 是一个 Next.js + TypeScript + MongoDB (Mongoose) 的 monorepo 项目

审计 MongoDB 应用时，我们需要关注的核心问题是：

用户输入是否被直接拼入 MongoDB 查询对象，而没有过滤以 $ 开头的操作符键？

这是 MongoDB + Node.js 应用中最常见的安全漏洞模式

先理解一下这个项目的架构

审计技巧 ①：在 Next.js 项目中，pages/api/ 目录下的每个文件就是一个 API 端点。文件路径即路由路径。这是你的审计入口清单

在 Mongoose 应用中，数据流通常是：

审计目标：在每一层检查用户输入是否被正确校验和净化，才能流向数据库查询。

定位 API 入口

前面讲过要审计的点是getHistories.ts，所在的路径是 FastGPT-4.13.0/projects/app/src/pages/api/core/chat/getHistories.ts

这个文件是后端处理逻辑的一个api接口

于是就开始看到getHistories.ts中的代码

在const { offset, pageSize } = parsePaginationRequest(req);前面的那些代码里面定义了几种规则URL参数规则，请求体规则，返回数据规则，处理函数规则，数据提取规则。const { offset, pageSize } = parsePaginationRequest(req);代码就是处理好offset, pageSize这里两个参数，没有什么好讲的

后面就来到了一个关键的代码了

具体看到

如果shareid和outlinkuid存在则，authoutlink函数经过处理之后得到uid，然后将outlinkuid的值替换为刚刚得到的uid

审计到了这里很明显就发现了一些问题

问题一：req.body 直接解构，无 Zod/schema 校验，用户可以传入任意 JSON 类型（对象、数组等）

问题二：shareId 直接写入 match 对象， 如果 shareId 是 {"$ne": ""}，MongoDB 会解释为操作符

问题三：outLinkUid: uid — uid 来自 authOutLink()，需要追踪这个函数返回的 uid 是否安全

于是开始审计 authOutLink 函数

追踪认证链authOutLink

authOutLink 被调用来验证 shareId 和 outLinkUid。打开 FastGPT-4.13.0/projects/app/src/service/support/permission/auth/outLink.ts：

对于这个代码，具体要看的内容肯定是authOutLink函数所在的代码

这个代码片段

定义收到的hareId,outLinkUid的数据类型是ShareChatAuthProps，返回的数据类型是Promise

后面直接看outLinkUid存在的处理逻辑

const result = await authOutLinkValid({ shareId });这个代码清晰的写了shareid丢给了authOutLinkValid函数进行处理，处理之后得到result变量

来到后面

用 outLinkUid（用户给的外链凭证）和 hookUrl（验证接口地址）去调用 authOutLinkInit 函数，从返回结果里取出 uid（真实用户ID）

所以对于这个代码来说是不是有两个验证，一个是authOutLinkValid一个是authOutLinkInit
他们两个的验证是息息相关的authOutLinkValid接收shareId输出result，authOutLinkInit接收outLinkUid和有关result的值输出最终需要的uid

审计到了这里就又发现了几个问题

问题一：检查outlinkuid是否为空if (!outLinkUid)，如果输入的是对象的话是可以绕过truthy 检查的

问题二：后续需要具体的审计一下authOutLinkValid和authOutLinkInit的处理逻辑

追踪认证链authOutLinkValid

函数所在的位置

packages/service/support/permission/publish/authLink.ts

具体的代码如下

现在我们开始来到了另外的一个伪协议php://input

php://input 是 PHP 的内置伪协议（不是真实文件），它的核心作用是：读取 POST 请求的原始数据（不经过 PHP 解析）

使用可以把POST 请求发过来的原始数据直接读取到

如果只是需要读取数据的话allow_url_include = Off就可以了，但是我相信ctfer更愿意后者，执行代码allow_url_include = On

为什么可以使用这个进行文件包含

php://input 是 PHP 的内置伪协议，它并非指向真实文件，而是直接映射到本次 HTTP 请求的 POST 原始数据体（非 GET 参数，也非表单键值对的解析后数据）。当把 php://input 作为 “文件名” 传给包含函数时，PHP 会把 POST 原始数据当作 “文件内容” 读取，进而解析执行其中的 PHP 代码 —— 相当于跳过了读取服务器本地文件的步骤，直接让 PHP 执行你通过 POST 提交的任意代码。

在详细的讲使用之前我们先看看注意事项

enctype=”multipart/form-data” 时使用php://input是无效的

enctype 是 HTML 表单的属性，用来指定表单数据提交的编码方式，一共有四种方式

  • application/x-www-form-urlencoded：默认值，普通表单提交（键值对）；
  • multipart/form-data：用于上传文件（比如<input type="file">），数据会被分割成 “块” 传输。

为什么这种编码下 php://input 无效？
PHP 的设计规则：
当 POST 请求的Content-Type是multipart/form-data（即表单设了enctype="multipart/form-data“）时，PHP 会把 POST 数据解析到$_FILES/$_POST中，同时清空 php://input 的内容；
此时读取php://input会得到空字符串，自然无法执行你提交的代码。

不过还好的是在请求的时候默认使用的是

在PHP中，有一个register_argc_argv指令。当它开启时（在Docker的PHP镜像中默认开启），HTTP请求的查询字符串（Query String）（即?之后的部分）会被PHP解析，并存入$_SERVER[‘argv’]数组中。更关键的是，它会以加号（+）作为参数分隔符，而不是常规的&。这就像是给Web环境装上了命令行参数解析器。

pearcmd.php是PEAR（PHP扩展与应用仓库）的核心文件，本质上是PEAR命令行工具的入口。在Docker环境中，它几乎总是存在的，路径通常是/usr/local/lib/php/pearcmd.php。当它被文件包含漏洞加载时，它内部的readPHPArgv函数会优先读取我们可控的$_SERVER[‘argv’]作为其命令行参数。

entry.title: Hexo Fluid 主题测试文章（AI看法专题）
entry.content:
前言

随着生成式AI、大模型技术的快速迭代，人工智能已渗透到社会生活的方方面面，从日常聊天的AI助手、办公场景的智能创作，到工业生产的自动化控制、医疗领域的辅助诊断，AI正在深刻改变我们的生活与工作方式。与此同时，社会对AI的看法也呈现出多元分化的态势——有人拥抱其高效便捷，有人担忧其带来的伦理与就业挑战，有人保持理性观望。本文结合Hexo Fluid主题支持的全部格式，全面呈现当下社会对AI的各类看法，同时完成主题功能测试。

一、标题层级测试（AI看法分类）

1.1 积极看法：AI是提升效率的“赋能者”

1.1.1 办公与创作领域：降低门槛，提升产能

在当下职场中，AI已成为许多人的“高效搭档”。无论是文案创作、PPT制作，还是数据整理、翻译润色，AI工具都能快速完成基础工作，让人们将精力聚焦于更具创造性的核心任务。例如，新媒体从业者可借助AI生成文案初稿，设计师可通过AI辅助生成创意草图，程序员可利用AI排查代码bug，大幅缩短工作周期。

这种赋能不仅体现在专业领域，也惠及普通大众——学生可通过AI辅助学习、解答疑问，老年人可借助AI语音助手解决操作难题，普通人也能通过AI快速掌握新技能，实现“人人皆可高效产出”的可能。

1.1.2 民生与公共领域：优化体验，解决痛点

在民生领域，AI的应用正在破解诸多传统难题：智能导航让出行更便捷，AI医疗辅助诊断能提高基层医疗机构的诊断准确率，智能安防系统提升了公共安全水平，AI垃圾分类、智能水电调控则助力绿色低碳生活。这些应用让人们的生活更便捷、更高效，也让公共服务更具普惠性。

1.2 担忧看法：AI带来的“挑战与隐患”

1.2.1 就业冲击：部分岗位面临被替代风险

这是社会对AI最普遍的担忧之一。随着AI自动化技术的发展，重复性、机械性的岗位（如数据录入、简单排版、基础客服、流水线作业等）面临被AI替代的风险，导致部分从业者面临失业压力。尤其是低技能劳动者，如何适应AI时代的就业变革，成为当下亟待解决的问题。

有人认为，AI替代岗位的同时会创造新的岗位（如AI训练师、AI运维师），但岗位转型需要时间和技能储备，短期内的就业冲击仍不可忽视。

1.2.2 伦理与安全：潜在风险不容忽视

AI的快速发展也带来了一系列伦理与安全隐患：

  • 信息安全：AI生成内容（如DeepFake视频、虚假文案）可能被用于造谣、诈骗，误导公众；

  • 隐私泄露：AI模型训练需要大量数据，若数据收集和使用不规范，可能侵犯个人隐私；

  • 伦理边界：AI决策的公平性（如招聘、贷款中的AI算法歧视）、AI创作的版权归属等问题，目前仍缺乏明确的规范和界定。

1.3 理性看法：辩证看待，趋利避害

多数理性观点认为，AI本身是一种工具，其影响取决于人类如何使用它。既不能盲目追捧AI的“万能性”，也不能过度放大其“危害性”，而应辩证看待、趋利避害——发挥AI在提升效率、解决难题上的优势，同时通过完善法律法规、规范技术应用，防范其潜在风险。

需要明确的是，AI无法替代人类的情感、创造力和判断力，无论是艺术创作、情感沟通，还是复杂的决策判断，人类的核心价值始终无法被AI取代。

二、列表测试（AI相关场景分类）

2.1 无序列表：AI的主要应用场景

  • 办公场景：AI文案、AI表格、AI会议纪要

  • 生活场景：AI语音助手、AI导航、AI购物推荐

  • 专业场景：

    • 医疗AI：辅助诊断、药物研发

    • 工业AI：自动化生产、设备巡检

    • 教育AI：个性化辅导、作业批改

  • 创作场景：AI绘画、AI音乐、AI小说

2.2 有序列表：社会对AI的认知演变

  1. 初期好奇：AI技术刚出现时，人们对其充满好奇，主要关注其“新奇功能”（如语音对话、图像识别）；

  2. 快速接受：随着AI工具的普及，人们逐渐习惯其存在，将其应用于日常工作和生活；

  3. 理性反思：当AI带来的就业冲击、伦理问题逐渐显现，人们开始反思其潜在风险；

  4. 规范发展：各国开始出台相关政策，规范AI技术应用，推动AI健康、可持续发展。

三、代码块测试（AI相关代码示例）
